title: CORS, CSP and the same-origin policy: retrieval check
markdown:
## Recall before you check

This retrieval pass revisits the browser security model without re-teaching it. Before opening the check, say in your own words what an origin is (scheme, host, port), what the same-origin policy blocks by default and what it does not, how CORS lets a server opt a cross-origin reader in with response headers, when the browser sends a preflight `OPTIONS` request, what `credentials: 'include'` requires of the server, and what a Content Security Policy restricts and reports.

## What to bring back

- Two URLs share an origin only when scheme, host and port all match; `https://app.example` and `https://api.example` are different origins.
- The same-origin policy blocks reading cross-origin responses from scripts; it does not block sending simple requests or loading images and scripts.
- CORS is enforced by the browser from response headers such as `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`; the request still reaches the server.
- A preflight happens for non-simple requests: methods beyond GET/HEAD/POST, custom headers, or content types other than the three simple ones.
- With credentials, the server must echo a specific origin and send `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`; a wildcard is rejected.
- CSP restricts which sources may load or execute; `report-to` or `report-uri` sends violation reports, and `script-src` with nonces or hashes replaces inline allowances.

Answer from memory first, then read the feedback.

key_takeaways: An origin is scheme, host and port; CORS is enforced by the browser on the response.
Preflights come from non-simple methods, headers or content types.
CSP allows sources and reports violations; nonces or hashes replace unsafe-inline.

questions.prompt: Which pair of URLs shares an origin?
questions.explanation: Only the path differs; scheme, host and port are identical.

questions.prompt: A cross-origin `fetch` fails with a CORS error in the console. What actually happened?
choices: The request never left the browser
The request reached the server, but the response lacked headers allowing this origin to read it
The browser blocked all cross-origin traffic
questions.correct_answer: The request reached the server, but the response lacked headers allowing this origin to read it
questions.explanation: CORS gates reading the response in script; it is enforced from response headers.
questions.learning_objective: Explain what a CORS failure means

questions.prompt: Which request triggers a preflight OPTIONS?
questions.explanation: PUT and application/json are outside the simple-request rules.

questions.prompt: A credentialed cross-origin request needs which server response?
choices: A specific Access-Control-Allow-Origin plus Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
questions.correct_answer: A specific Access-Control-Allow-Origin plus Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
questions.explanation: Wildcards are rejected for credentialed requests.

questions.prompt: What replaces `'unsafe-inline'` for scripts in a Content Security Policy?
choices: Nonces or hashes on the allowed inline scripts
Moving scripts to a different origin
questions.correct_answer: Nonces or hashes on the allowed inline scripts
questions.explanation: A nonce or hash allows specific inline scripts without opening all inline execution.
